'''Donte DiVincenzo''' (born January 31, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]]. He won national championships with Villanova in [[2016 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2016]] and [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018]].

==Early life and high school career==
DiVincenzo was born in [[Newark, Delaware]], the son of John F. and Kathie DiVincenzo and has an older brother, John A.<ref name="villanova"/> Donte focused on soccer growing up before focusing exclusively on basketball in high school.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Schonbrun|first1=Zach|title=Donte DiVincenzo and Trevon Duval Give Delaware Hoops a Moment|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/23/sports/delaware-march-madness.html|accessdate=March 31, 2018|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 23, 2018}}</ref> He attended the [[Salesianum School]], where he led the team to two consecutive state championships. As a junior, he averaged 15.8 points, 4.7 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game and played basketball in the Nike EYBL for Team Final. DiVincenzo averaged 22.9 points, 9.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game as a senior. He was named Delaware Sportswriters and Broadcasters Association's Boys' Basketball Player of the Year in 2015.<ref name="villanova">{{cite web|title=10 Donte DiVincenzo|url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/donte_divincenzo_979537.html|website=[[Villanova Wildcats]]|accessdate=March 31, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Villanova Parade 2018 04.jpg|file|thumb|right|250px|[[Eric Paschall]], DiVincenzo, [[Omari Spellman]], [[Collin Gillespie]], and [[Jalen Brunson]].]]
DiVincenzo appeared in eight games his true freshman year for Villanova before sitting out with a fractured fifth metatarsal bone in his right foot. The following season, in his [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] freshman season, DiVincenzo averaged 8.8 points and 3.8 rebounds per game. He registered 19 points, three rebounds and two assists in a 70–57 victory against [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] on January 14, 2017. On March 9, DiVincenzo had a season-high 25 points to go with five rebounds and four assists in a 108–67 rematch win over St. John's. In the NCAA Tournament, he scored 21 points and grabbed 13 rebounds in a 76–56 victory over [[Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball|Mount St. Mary's]] in the first round. DiVincenzo was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Freshman team and the [[Philadelphia Big 5|Philadelphia Big Five]] Rookie of the Year.<ref name="villanova"/> 

In his redshirted sophomore season, DiVincenzo had a then career-high 30 points in a 86–75 win over [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] on February 10, 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Donte DiVincenzo, Jalen Brunson lead Villanova past Butler|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988606|accessdate=March 31, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 10, 2018}}</ref> At the conclusion of the regular season, he was named Big East Sixth Man of the Year.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Juliano|first1=Joe|title=Villanova's Donte DiVincenzo wins Big East Sixth Man award|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/villanova-big-east-basketball-donte-divincenzo-ncaa-tournament-20180305.html|accessdate=March 31, 2018|work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 5, 2018}}</ref> In the Elite Eight of the 2018 NCAA Tournament, DiVincenzo had 12 points and eight rebounds in a 71–59 win over [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Smallwood|first1=John|title=Villanova's Donte DiVincenzo and Eric Paschall more than spectators for this Final Four team|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/villanova-march-madness-final-four-donte-divincenzo-eric-paschall-ncaa-tournament-20180326.html|accessdate=March 31, 2018|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 26, 2018}}</ref> DiVincenzo was named the NCAA Final Four Most Outstanding Player following their championship win over Michigan, after a career game where he scored a new career-high 31 points (including five three-point baskets), had five rebounds, three assists and blocked two shots. In addition, he scored the most points in an NCAA Final Four game for a player coming off the bench.<ref>[http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23007836/villanova-donte-divincenzo-wins-most-outstanding-player-final-four "Villanova's Donte DiVincenzo named Most Outstanding Player"]. espn.com. April 3, 2018. Retrieved April 3, 2018.</ref>

DiVincenzo was dubbed the "Big [[Ragù|Ragu]]" by sportscaster [[Gus Johnson (sportscaster)|Gus Johnson]] following his last-second tip in a game on January 29, 2017, which gave Villanova the win against the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|University of Virginia]]. The nickname was given to him ostensibly due to his Italian heritage and his red hair.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/who-is-donte-divincenzo-all-you-need-to-know-about-villanovas-big-ragu/|title=Who is Donte DiVincenzo? All you need to know about Villanova's 'Big Ragu'|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=April 3, 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/04/02/villanova-donte-divincenzo-fast-facts|title=What you need to Know about Villanova’s Donte DiVincenzo|work=SI.com|access-date=April 3, 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2018/04/donte-divincenzo-big-ragu|title=This is how Donte DiVincenzo got the nickname 'The Big Ragu'|work=ftw.usatoday.com|access-date=April 9, 2018|language=en}}</ref> On April 19, 2018, DiVincenzo announced he would declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]] without hiring an agent, thereby leaving open the possibility of a return to Villanova. On May 29, 2018, DiVincenzo announced he would remain in the draft and hire an agent, forgoing his final two years of eligibility at Villanova.
